diagnostic_evidence.quote: Assume that there exists $\z_0 \in \R^\N$ with $\A\z_0 = \y$ and set $\w_0 = \0$.

issues.failure_explanation: For the tanh link/reparametrization, the range is (-1, 1)^N. Assuming merely that there exists z_0 in R^N such that A z_0 = y does not guarantee the existence of any z in R^N satisfying L(z) = 0 (i.e., A tanh(z) = y); if y is not in A((-1, 1)^N), the feasible set {z in R^N : L(z) = 0} is empty. Furthermore, g_tanh(z) = <z, artanh(z)> is undefined whenever any component of z lies outside (-1, 1), yet the optimization is taken over unconstrained z in R^N with L(z) = 0. The implicit regularization applies to the reparametrized variable wtilde_infty = lim tanh(w(t)), so the objective should be g_tanh(rho_rp(z)) = g_tanh(tanh(z)) or minimized over ztilde in [-1, 1]^N.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Strengthen the hypothesis of Theorem 1.4 to assume the existence of ztilde_0 in (-1, 1)^N such that A ztilde_0 = y (Assumption (B2)), and correct the formula in statement 2 to min_{z in R^N, L(z)=0} g_tanh(rho_rp(z)) (or equivalently min_{ztilde in [-1,1]^N, L_tilde(ztilde)=0} g_tanh(ztilde)).
issues.overall_effect: Part 2 of Theorem 1.4 is mathematically ill-defined as written, and its feasible set is empty whenever the linear observation y cannot be generated by coefficients in (-1, 1)^N.
issues.title: Invalid premise and ill-defined objective in tanh implicit regularization statement
issues.why_classification: Restricting the solvable data regime to the natural range of tanh and repairing the formula to act on the reparametrized variable are standard local corrections matching the paper's later statements in Corollaries 2.7 and 2.8, leaving the architecture and advertised results intact.

issues.failure_explanation: Theorem 2.4 states that under Assumptions (B1), (A2), (A3), and (B2), the convergence rates (i), (ii), and trajectory convergence (iii) hold. However, Assumption (A3) only assumes that L is C^1 and has a unique minimum value 0 at z = z'. The proof of Lemma 3.2, upon which Theorem 2.4 entirely depends, uses the first-order condition of convexity for v -> L(v, y) to establish d/dt D_F(ztilde_0, wtilde(t)) <= -L_tilde(wtilde(t)). Without convexity of L(., y), this inequality fails, and gradient flow on L_tilde can be trapped in non-global local minima or saddle points, invalidating claims (i), (ii), and (iii).

failure_location.quote: Assume that \johannes{Assumptions \ref{as:B1}, \ref{as:A2}, \ref{as:A3}, and \ref{as:B2} hold and recall} from Theorem \ref{theorem:vector_IRERM} the function $h$ defined in \eqref{eq:hprimedefinitionWithoutPositivity} and the Bregman divergence $D_F$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the explicit hypothesis to Assumption (A3) or Theorem 2.4 that v -> L(v, y) is convex.
issues.overall_effect: All claims in Theorem 2.4 (the 1/t rate, the linear convergence rate under PL, and the convergence of bounded trajectories to zero loss) as well as its specific applications in Corollaries 2.6 and 2.8 become unestablished for general non-convex loss functions satisfying (A3).
issues.title: Omission of convexity of loss function in convergence guarantees
issues.why_classification: Convexity of L is standard in generalized linear models and is already mentioned informally in the prose preceding Theorem 2.4; adding this standard local condition validates Lemma 3.2 and Theorem 2.4 without changing proof architecture or advertised scope.

issues.failure_explanation: For p <= 1, the derivative of the mirror map satisfies h(0) = -infinity, so Theorem 2.3 can only be applied if wtilde_{infty, alpha} is strictly positive (in int(D_rp)). The proof of Corollary 3.3 claims this holds by invoking Lemma 3.2. However, Lemma 3.2 requires Assumption (B2) (the existence of a strictly positive ztilde_0 with A ztilde_0 = y), which is not assumed in Corollary 2.5. If all solutions in R_{>=0}^N lie on the boundary, wtilde_{infty, alpha} must have zero entries, meaning neither condition (i) nor (ii) of Theorem 2.3 is satisfied. In addition, Corollary 2.5 does not assume that L_tilde(wtilde_{infty, alpha}) = 0, which is an explicit premise of Theorem 2.3.

failure_location.quote: Define $\wprod_0 = \sigmainn(\w_0) = \alpha \bo$, for $\alpha > 0$, and assume that $\wprod_{\infty,\alpha} := \lim_{\t \to \infty} \sigmainn(\w(\t))$ exists for any $\alpha$ sufficiently small.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add Assumption (B2) (the existence of ztilde_0 in int(D_rp) with A ztilde_0 = y) and the premise L_tilde(wtilde_{infty, alpha}) = 0 to the hypotheses of Corollary 2.5 and Corollary 3.3.
issues.overall_effect: Corollaries 2.5 and 3.3 are unestablished when no strictly positive solution to A ztilde = y exists, or when gradient flow converges to a stationary point with non-zero loss.
issues.title: Omission of Assumption (B2) and global optimality of the limit in polynomial regularization
issues.why_classification: Adding Assumption (B2) (which was already stated in Theorem 1.3 and Corollary 2.6) and zero loss of the limit are local standard hypotheses that immediately complete the argument of Corollary 3.3 without altering the core technique.
